tgt_statement_en: POV forks are not permitted on Wikipedia.
The NPOV policy is non-negotiable and cannot be superseded by other policies, guidelines, or editor consensus.
A single name should be chosen as the article title even when multiple terms are in common usage, in line with the article titling policy.
NPOV does not mean excluding points of view; it means including all verifiable points of view that have sufficient due weight.
Bias problems should be fixed when possible through the normal editing process, balancing biased material with material from other sources.
A POV fork is an attempt to evade the neutrality policy by creating a new article about a subject already treated in an existing article.
Undue weight can be given through depth of detail, quantity of text, prominence of placement, juxtaposition of statements, and use of imagery.
Coverage of beliefs and practices should encompass both what motivates their adherents and how those beliefs and practices developed.
No words or expressions are forbidden on Wikipedia, but certain expressions should be used with care because they may introduce bias.
Segregating content into regions or subsections based solely on its apparent point of view may produce an unencyclopedic structure and should be avoided.
A little-believed theory may be appropriately included once it has been presented and discussed in reliable sources.
The preference for nonjudgmental language must sometimes be balanced against clarity.
